title: Rare · breeds few people keep
blurb: Small registries and island populations: the breeds that survived a handful of founders and are still counted in hundreds, not millions.

items.d: A Kenyan forest cat from the Arabuko-Sokoke forest, with a ticked coat and no tail problems.
Singapore's small ticked cat, one of the smallest breeds, at 2–3 kg.
A Burmese and Persian accident from 1981, with a silver shaded coat and a calm temper.
Australia's own breed, 1976: a spotted and marbled shorthair with a gentle, indoor manner.
An American spotted shorthair bred from Abyssinian, Siamese and American Shorthair lines.
A longhaired Russian Blue type from the 1980s, named after a German mist.
The large, placid longhair split from the Ragdoll in the 1990s, in every colour.
The desert cat of the Gulf, recognised in 2008 from the street cats of the Arabian peninsula.
